content.text:
I submitted index 0 (Ca 0.14 / Fe 0.70 / Mn 0.16), but the campaign found no working photoanode: all three measurements gave essentially zero photocurrent.

| Index | Region | Composition (Ca/Fe/Mn) | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Fe-rich (like hematite, Fe₂O₃) | 0.14 / 0.70 / 0.16 | −0.0 A |
| 104 | Ca-rich | 0.59 / 0.24 / 0.17 | −6e-8 A |
| 94 | Mixed centre | 0.25 / 0.48 / 0.27 | −0.0 A |

- **Why index 0:** it ties with index 94 for the highest reading. I picked it because it had the best case going in: the band-gap model puts hematite's gap at 2.77 eV (HSE) or 1.53 eV (PBE), near or below the 2.72 eV light, so it should absorb.
- **Mn-rich compositions:** I didn't measure any. The model predicts the Mn₂O₃ analogue is nearly metallic (0.015 eV gap), so they're unlikely to work as photoanodes.
- **Unused tools:** the GP model couldn't rank candidates after the first zero, and I used none of the 5 XRD measurements. I also never read the full phase list, which was too large to return directly, so my picks rest on hematite and one substituted structure.

With only 3 measurements across 183 candidates, the best composition may simply be somewhere I didn't test. Since my submission scored about zero, the score will likely be poor unless the whole library is inactive under these conditions.
